entity: SEC Division of Investment Management -- Private Fund Statistics
finding: Confirms the structural reason no data-center-specific series can exist: SEC's own quarterly aggregate Form PF report categorizes the 58,891 private funds reported for 2025Q4 (the latest published quarter) ONLY by legal fund TYPE -- Private Equity Fund, Hedge Fund, Other Private Fund, Real Estate Fund, Venture Capital Fund, Securitized Asset Fund, Liquidity Fund. Full-text search of the entire 69-page PDF report: zero occurrences of 'data center' or 'digital infrastructure' anywhere. The taxonomy is by fund legal structure, not by underlying portfolio-company industry, so a sector-level data-center breakout is not something this report could show even if such exposure exists.

entity: Ares Capital Corp (ARCC) -- same borrower, separate commitment

source_type: BDC 10-K (public, risk factor only -- no named holding found)
finding: BCRED (the largest private-credit BDC-like vehicle checked) carries a data-center-specific RISK FACTOR: 'We may make investments related to data centers, which exposes us to related risks... in the data center industry, which exposes us to risks inherent in that sector,' plus a separate passage flagging that 'private credit supports cross-investments among artificial intelligence- and data center-focused firms.' This signals actual or anticipated exposure, but keyword search of the full filing found no 'data center' text inside the Schedule of Investments itself, i.e. no specific data-center borrower was identifiable by name via this method (a holding classified under a different industry label, e.g. 'Internet Services,' would not have been caught).

Describes its manager's (Blue Owl's) broader 'Real Assets' platform as covering 'digital infrastructure, which focuses on acquiring, financing, developing and operating data centers,' and states OTF itself 'may evaluate cross-platform opportunities to invest in data center assets and AI related equipment such as graphic processing units' -- forward-looking/aspirational language, not a current named holding.

Full-text search for '"data center" "Schedule of Investments"' restricted to Form 10-K returned 27 hits across named BDC/private-credit filers (Ares Capital, Main Street Capital, MSC Income Fund, Blackstone Secured Lending Fund, Blackstone Private Credit Fund, Blue Owl Technology Finance/Income, Oaktree Strategic Credit Fund, Oaktree Specialty Lending, Sound Point Direct Lending BDC, Stonepeak-Plus Infrastructure Fund, Blackstone Infrastructure Strategies, and others) -- used only to identify candidates for direct reading (per project HTTP rules, full-text search hit counts are not used as a filing count anywhere in this CSV).

The original note's claim -- 'no [data-center-specific private-credit] series exists anywhere' -- is CONFIRMED for aggregate/series-level data (Form PF statistics cannot show it; no such published series was found anywhere in bounded searching). It is NOT confirmed that private credit has zero data-center exposure: Ares Capital Corp's public 10-K provides a genuine, named, quantified first data point (Vantage Data Centers, ~$40mn funded + ~$155mn undrawn commitment), and Blackstone's BCRED explicitly flags data-center investment as a live risk category. Effort was bounded per the brief; a full census of all ~200+ SEC-registered BDCs' schedules of investments was NOT attempted.
